(V)accination (T)imeliness Distribution

Source: R/vt_distribution.R
vt_distribution.Rd

This function calculates the probabilistic version of the vaccination timeliness analysis: the distribution of vaccinations by number of days elapsed since the start of the timeliness window (age_schedule_low), further disaggregating by geographic level, using data from the electronic immunization registry (EIR). It returns, for each day, the empirical probability density (pdf), i.e. the percentage of records vaccinated on that day, and the empirical cumulative distribution (cdf), i.e. the percentage of records vaccinated up to that day.

Usage

vt_distribution(
  data.EIR,
  data.schedule,
  geo_level = "ADM0",
  vaccines = NULL,
  birth_cohorts = NULL
)

Arguments

data.EIR

Data frame. A data frame containing individual vaccination records. See pahoabc.EIR for expected structure.

data.schedule

Data frame. A data frame defining the vaccination schedule. See pahoabc.schedule for expected structure.

geo_level

Character. The geographic level to aggregate results by. Must be "ADM0", "ADM1" or "ADM2". If not specified, the default is "ADM0".

vaccines

Character (optional). A character vector specifying the doses to include in the analysis, disaggregating results by dose. If NULL (default), all doses in data.schedule are included and pooled together.

birth_cohorts

Numeric (optional). A vector specifying the birth cohort(s) for which the distribution should be calculated. If NULL (default), all available cohorts are pooled together. Note that the most recent cohorts may not have had time to receive late vaccinations, which biases the distribution towards faster vaccination; consider excluding cohorts with incomplete follow-up. Specifying cohorts also excludes records with no date_birth, so n_missing may be undercounted.

Value

A data frame with one row per day since the start of the timeliness window, with the following columns:

  • day: days since the start of the timeliness window (age_schedule_low).

  • n: number of records vaccinated on that day.

  • pdf: percentage of records vaccinated on that day.

  • cum_n: cumulative number of records vaccinated up to that day.

  • cdf: cumulative percentage of records vaccinated up to that day.

  • n_at_risk: number of records not yet vaccinated at the start of that day (population "at risk").

  • total: number of vaccinations in the EIR for that dose and/or geographic area, excluding n_early and n_missing.

  • n_early: number of records vaccinated before the timeliness window, excluded from total.

  • n_missing: number of records with a missing date, excluded from total.

  • window_end: last timely day (age_schedule_high - age_schedule_low); NA when doses are pooled.

Details

Day 0 corresponds to age_schedule_low, so records vaccinated before the timeliness window (n_early) are excluded from the distribution and from its denominator (total), as are records with a missing date (n_missing). Because of this, the cdf at window_end is not equal to the TIMELY rate from vt_rate, which keeps early records in its denominator. Also note that, since only vaccinated records are analyzed, the cdf always reaches 100%, which overestimates the probability of vaccination of the whole target population.
